headline: British Museum director Nicholas Cullinan: 'The Bayeux Tapestry, in a non-nationalistic way, is clearly part of our national identity'
subhead: With just seven days to go before the exhibition opens, the director of the British Museum, Nicholas Cullinan, reflects on the extraordinary journey involved in the loan and transfer of this monumental work from France to England.

Netanyahu says security officials deliberately didn't wake him on October 7
subhead: On Tuesday, the Israeli prime minister insisted that Hamas's attacks on the morning of October 7, 2023, would have been contained if he had been woken earlier – but that his security officials intentionally failed to do so.

headline: Iran sentences photojournalist to 15 years in prison for sharing images of repression abroad
subhead: Accused of sending photographs abroad, Yalda Moaiery has just had her sentence upheld on appeal. In January, Le Monde published her images of the protests against the regime – a rare testimonial.

headline: The dangers of 'eating jet lag': Why eating at irregular hours is bad for your health
subhead: A large-scale French study suggests that men who eat meals at highly variable times between workdays and days off face an increased risk of cardiovascular disease.

headline: 'With France seeking profound change, momentum lies only with candidates who promise to upend the status quo'
subhead: As speculation mounts over a possible second-round duel between far-right Marine Le Pen and radical left Jean-Luc Mélenchon in the 2027 French presidential election, no candidate from a party that has previously governed has managed to break through. This situation is having damaging effects, writes Le Monde columnist Françoise Fressoz.

subhead: The renewed strikes between the United States and Iran on Monday, August 31, confirms that the conflict has become entrenched in these waters. Tehran's ability to use the blockade of this strategic artery as a deterrent is gradually weakening.
